citations.review_text: Game is dead. Can't find a match

This game looks nicee but it's NO LONGER SUPPORTED , it's buggy and it's dead.

There is basically no new community and as I've seen on discord - the most of new players just give up early because the game is no longer supported and matchmaking is awful.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the controls as utilizing cursor-based aiming that feels overly fickle when using a steam controller.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Ryan George Style Pitch Meeting:[/h1]

The setting is a floating, hyper-stylized arena hovering over a glowing pool of crystal-clear turquoise water. Neon-lit banners swing gently in the breeze. In the background, two elaborate top-down action figures wearing tiny cloaks are being catapulted across the room by an automated pneumatic launcher, crashing into a giant wall of glowing green health orbs with a soft pop. A dramatic fog machine blasts dense white mist across the floor every three seconds, forcing both men to fan the air with rolled-up design documents.

Publisher: So, you have a high-speed top-down action arena combat simulator where players immediately get thrown into a high-stress mechanical nightmare for me?

Game Designer: Yes, my splendid chum, I absolutely do! It’s called Battlerite! We drop players straight into a shrinking death vortex in Trial 2 and bombard them with instant-cast spell indicators!

Publisher: Wow. Won't new players get confused trying to learn how to aim and move at the exact same time?

Game Designer: Super easy, barely an inconvenience! We just give every single character nine different combat abilities right out of the gate!

Publisher: Nine?!

Game Designer: Nine! Left click, right click, Spacebar, Q, E, R, F, plus two Shift-modified EX variants! Your fingers will be doing high-speed acoustic guitar solos across the keyboard! And if you dare to attack while trying to dodge, your character slows down to a crawl!

Publisher: Wait, attacking slows down your movement speed? Does the tutorial explicitly inform the player about this crucial movement penalty?

Game Designer: Hey, shut up!

Publisher: Fair enough.

Game Designer: So anyway, there’s no farming, no laning, no items, and no gold! It’s just non-stop, 100% relentless teamfighting from the very first second!

Publisher: Oooooh, stripping away all downtime so players never get a single second to catch their breath is tight!

Game Designer: It is extremely tight! You enter…

Not giving my email address to games just to be sent spam. Got around it though somehow by closing and reopening the game because I was going to idle long enough to write a review. Decided to give it a try and enabled steam controller input but since its cursor based aiming was too fickle.

citations.review_text:
Makro yerine mikro oyuna odaklanan, zor bir moba. Arena-Mobası diyelim.

Point and click yetenekler yerine sadece skillshotlar var. LoL'deki AA bile yok oyunda. Yani baya zor. 

45.145 oyuncuya kadar ulaşmış, ancak sonradan ölmüş bir oyun. Şuan oyuncu sayısı 120'yi geçmez.
However it needs players :(
Does anyone still play this game?
Cute game too bad it has no playerbase
It’s a competitive game where the biggest challenge is finding an actual competitor. It’s like someone distilled the worst parts of MOBA and shoved them into an arena with no escape.
match making is too long why not combine 1v1 2v2 and 3v3 match making, takes so long, this what makes me quit from hero of storm and other great games ,

Played this game a lot when it first went into betas and prior to it being on steam. Unfortunately it never gained traction... And that still seems true today. Which is a shame. I actually love the element of a MOBA actually being a Battle Arena, and not lanes. Fighting mostly in a circle with walls blocking some visibility is great. It's a lot of fun. Character variety is mostly there.

...It's just the player base. The game can't keep an audience. It feels like the players who stick with it are fighting game type players rather than MOBA players. That would be fine, except they're just as toxic... A different kind of toxic.

Came back to play it on Steam after remembering it existed. Had a lot of fun in bots. Then got to regular matches... Almost every match was against the same handful of players. Every match was just people who knew each other flaming each other. Queues were regularly 5m or more for casual, and even then almost every match people would start disconnecting after round 1. I'd be lucky to make it to round two before someone D/C'd and make us wait even longer to get the thrashing we'd get over with... 

I really do hate to not recommend it, but I just don't think it's ever going to get the community it needs to thrive. I don't think it's the company's fault at all. I don't think it's a game design fault. I don't have a solution, but unless you've got the mental of ranked fighting games - It's probably not gonna be for you.

fun as fk but dead game
better to play early in the day for best player traffic

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from a very small playerbase and long queue times.

citations.review_text:
If you like games like Smite or League of Legends, maybe you should give Battlerite a try.
Here's what I think about the game:

Positives:
1) It runs well ( I haven't played this game in awhile but even back then, with a much weaker PC, the game still ran very well )
2) Fast satisfying combat where decisions, mechanics, timing and positioning matters a lot.
3) Simpler than other MOBAs ( You don't have to worry about objectives and all that jazz. You get in and you fight )
4) F2P so nothing is stopping you from giving it a chance.

Negatives:
1) Small playerbase. Which means you can take a nap before you will find a match sometimes. The queues can be very long
2) Related to the small playerbase and long queues; That makes the game look dead/dying
3) I haven't played it lately but back when I did, there weren't any updates or new content

I used to play this game with friends and it was soooo much fun. It makes me sad to see it die because I've got many good memories with it.
please someone revive this game already, only bad thing is queues

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the developers stopped updating the game and shifted focus to a battle royale project, which split the playerbase.

citations.review_text: mechanically this was one of the best games i'd ever played. it's a shame how they split the playerbase and then abandoned this game. i'm still getting email updates about stunlock's new projects. i would not play any of their games again due to how quickly they finish and then stop updating their projects.

Incredible game held captive by shortsighted devs that killed it whilst trying (and miserably failing) to chase the Battle Royale trend, splitting the dev team and thus killing both games in their infancy, unaware of the incredible game that they had already invented. sad story - play this game because it kicks ass!

It's honestly a shame that more people don't know the name Stunlock Studio. 

I feel like the lack of people talking about how badly they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ this up stems entirely from nobody realizing what they did. These guys had the best battle arena game ever, bar none, literally zero competition at the time or since that comes even remotely close and they blew it. TWICE.

Bloodline Champions was amazing. It died. Battlerite was a resurrection of Bloodline Champions under a new IP to 'escape the limitations of a publisher' and I was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ecstatic over that because it was everything I remembered and more. 

Guess how that played out? They let it die. And why did they let it die? Why, to chase Battle Royale money of course. What else? Make a new 'battle royale' mode in the dedicated arena pvp game, fail to deliver updates of any kind to the actual gameplay, and then make people pay for the 'new mode' because it's actually a new game and... oh hey look it didn't gain traction and died like the vast majority of other BRs that followed the trend. Who could have seen this coming?

It's just so frustrating, too, because they managed to still get rewarded for this behavior in the end by releasing V-Rising - see all those people praising how the combat feels in that game? 

I'll ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bet. I felt that same way when I first experienced it in Bloodline Champions, and I felt it all over again when I relived it in Battlerite during the early days when it was a glorious rise from the ashes. I'm sure there is more to V-Rising as a game, but without the combat they practically lifted directly from the game they abandoned I promise you it would not have been nearly as successful.

TLDR - I would love to recommend you this game. If it was in the hands of another studio, I probably would be wholeheartedly singing praises for it and would fall over myself in my haste to recommend it to literally anybody who would listen. But unfortunately, the game that I would - to this day! - call the d…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat as fast-paced arena action that removes MOBA elements like farming and item purchasing to focus entirely on team fighting.

citations.review_text: The best game this studio has ever made and in a sane world this would be more popular than LoL. Cuts out all the tedium in a dota-like and focuses on the fun part. I think this game could have played with more scaling within a match, nonetheless a fun game.

High skill ceiling, low barrier to entry. A game that rewards mechanical mastery and understanding. It feels like playing a MOBA, but you get to skip straight to the team fighting part. 

My absolute favourite competitive game, possibly ever. Unfortunately, the studio behind it was not willing to put any more effort into developing it and growing its competitive scene, so now it is dead. My friends and I still reminisce about how incredibly fun this game was.
was so sad to see this go. Jade<3
Simply the perfect game if you enjoy the fighting part of MOBAs but not the strategy and farming part

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as fast-paced combat centered around skillshots, reactions, and mechanics like animation canceling and baiting defensive abilities, without traditional MOBA elements like lane farming or item shops.

citations.review_text: Tight and intense gameplay requiring precision with skillshots and reacting to your opponent's moves.

Such an amazing game. 
The amount of times I've craved this game, it's fast paced moba 2v2/3v3 style where it felt so rewarding to outplay other players. The whole game was built on reactions and skill. Haven't played for years due to no Australian playerbase.

What I'd give to be able to play this game again with an active playerbase. I wish the devs would market this game once more to see if it pops off. Not sure how such a gem of a game died out. 

Uniquely the best of it's kind with the smoothest gameplay. 

The game was simple, but with so many fine details, being able to animation cancel, cancel your cast entirely, baiting out player's defensive abilities.... RIP Battlerite. 
Please come back :(

When this game came out it made me switch from league, i enjoyed it that much. no more 20 minutes of  farming,making a build. Just 5 minutes of pure action, cool characters with cool abilities. 
I had really high hopes for the game to the point i was thinking that i would be the league killer, from the sheer enjoyment from the game, hoping and expecting many different characters, maps, combinations and interactions. Sadly when the game started dying it was really disheartening to see how the queue times got longer and  even worse when the devs released the paid battle-royale mode which split the already dwindling player base. I hope that the devs will not give up on this game and looking at V rising success, they will come back with the needed experience and funds which will revive the game.
There are still community matches being made on their discord but they barely reach 100 players nowadays. 
I would recommend this to give this game a try maybe with friends since there is 1v1,2v2,3v3 so you can still enjoy it.

An arena style MOBA, which focuses on the things that matter ... pure, simple, adrenaline pumping skill-based combat.

No Lanes.
No weird over-complicated item-shops.

Just sweet sweet combat, with very cool characters.

I miss this game...

Battlerite is an absolute corker of a game. I’ve played my share of MOBAs old and new with most of my time has been put into League of Legends and Overwatch, so it’s no small feat for a game to waltz onto the scene and completely capture me. Battlerite does things right on so many levels that it’s hard to ignore. Games are fast, frenetic, packed with only the greatest moments of League or Dota without slogging through the 20-30 minutes of ‘filler’ gameplay like farming, pushing lanes, and so forth. It carves out the high intensity combat from those games, gives it the skill-based aiming and movement of a FPS, and packages it beautifully together.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the developers abandoned the arena game to focus on developing a separate battle royale mode.

citations.review_text:
While working i randomly remembered about this game so i thought I'd write a review while in my copium-filled fervor in hopes that the game gets revived, inspires another developer to make a successor, or a sequel comes out.

Unfortunately as stated earlier, this is hopium spliced with copium, because once i saw that LoL made a similar gamemode I figured that cemented battlerite's end considering LoL players will only play the version of a game riot decides to attempt so the one demographic it could've garnered interest from is pretty much cutoff.

I didn't grow up playing too much bloodline champions but i knew about it from a smaller streamer, got super interested in it to try out bloodline champs, got obliterated, and then found that battlerite was its upcoming successor. 

Playing the closed alpha and its full release showed that the game was so much fun and had crazy mind-games plus skill expression, so there was so much potential for competition. Character roles were defined but not confined, as any one character seemed like they could carry if you played your cards right. 

I feel like the developers were on the right track up until the battle royal craze in which they, mistakenly, thought putting all their focus and resources into putting out a battle royale would help funnel people into the arena game to eventually put resources back into it. Well that idea flopped, and when the battle royale flopped it took arena with it as the developers discontinued its development immediately.

All in all, this legacy game's comeback had a strong start and was a great time while it had a decent pool of players until the battle royal craze happened causing the developers flying too close to the sun to benefit of a trend.

On another note, definitely try v-rising. The feel of battlerite is all there and they made an excellent vampire, survival, rpg that can be played like rust with raids and wipes or just as a singleplayer rpg experience. But Hopefully stunlock decides to…

Missed this game so much lately, sad the devs made the worst possible decisions again and again, basically killing the game in the process (battlerite royale, made to capitalize in the growing battleroyale genre at the time, was the biggest mistake by far)

As everyone else i hope to see a revival of some kind or a battlerite 2.

This game had so much potential from the start. I actually quit League of Legends for a while to play this game instead. It offered great character design and combat features that have unfortunately gone to waste. 

This game has been abandoned by its developers and player base after they put all their resources into the failed Battle Royale mode. I still check back every once in a while in hopes it will make a comeback.
good, unique game. sad that the devs killed it during battle royale phase

Pure skill and action.

Really, one of the best games in its genre killed by devs themselves chasing the battle royale goose..

We need Battlerite 2 in 2026 :(

claims.claim: Reviewers report extremely long queue times due to a depleted player base.

citations.review_text:
Battlerite is one of the most mechanically satisfying PVP games I have ever played. The combat is sharp, every move feels deliberate and rewarding, and the skill ceiling is high enough that 100+ hours in you are still finding new ways to outplay your opponents. Stunlock Studios built something genuinely special here and the depth of the mechanics keeps every match feeling competitive and engaging.

One thing that truly hurts:
1- The queue times are longer than a full 9 to 5 shift. You could clock in, complete a full workday, and still be waiting for a match. For a game this good, that is a tragedy.
8/10 an outstanding PVP experience let down by a dying player base. If the queues were healthy this would be a 9 without question.

When this game came out it made me switch from league, i enjoyed it that much. no more 20 minutes of  farming,making a build. Just 5 minutes of pure action, cool characters with cool abilities. 
I had really high hopes for the game to the point i was thinking that i would be the league killer, from the sheer enjoyment from the game, hoping and expecting many different characters, maps, combinations and interactions. Sadly when the game started dying it was really disheartening to see how the queue times got longer and  even worse when the devs released the paid battle-royale mode which split the already dwindling player base. I hope that the devs will not give up on this game and looking at V rising success, they will come back with the needed experience and funds which will revive the game.
There are still community matches being made on their discord but they barely reach 100 players nowadays. 
I would recommend this to give this game a try maybe with friends since there is 1v1,2v2,3v3 so you can still enjoy it.
